restated_task: Implement the is_balanced(s) function in brackets/core.py to check whether all parentheses (), square brackets [], and curly braces {} in the input string s are correctly matched and properly nested, ignoring any non-bracket characters. The function must return a boolean (True for balanced, False otherwise), raise TypeError if s is not a string, and treat the empty string as balanced. The existing is_bracket helper and the constants PAIRS, OPEN, CLOSE must remain unchanged.

interface_contract.name: is_balanced
interface_contract.behavior: Returns True if every opening bracket in s has a corresponding closing bracket of the same type in the correct order (properly nested), and there are no unmatched closing brackets. Non-bracket characters are ignored. The empty string returns True. The function must return a bool.
error_cases: TypeError: raised when s is not a string.

interface_contract.name: is_bracket
interface_contract.behavior: Returns True if c is a single-character string and one of the six bracket characters '(', ')', '[', ']', '{', '}'. Returns False for any other input (including non-strings, empty string, or multi-character strings). This function is already implemented and must not be modified.

acceptance_criteria: Non-bracket characters are ignored: is_balanced('a') returns True, is_balanced('(a)') returns True.
is_balanced returns a bool (True or False) for all valid string inputs.
is_balanced raises TypeError when s is not a string (e.g., is_balanced(123), is_balanced(None), is_balanced([1,2])).
The existing is_bracket behavior is preserved (as verified by the existing tests).
out_of_scope: Do not modify the is_bracket function.
Do not modify the PAIRS, OPEN, CLOSE constants.
Do not modify the test files (tests/test_basic.py).
Do not change the module structure or public exports in brackets/__init__.py.
